reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin AUS2-AUS3 campus publishes 19 MW of IT capacity, tenth among the 19 Texas facilities that disclose capacity and about four percent of the state's 475 MW.

The shape is a general-purpose colocation campus rather than an AI build. Its certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, qualify it for regulated enterprise workloads but say nothing about power density or cooling. The 19 MW is spread across 242,000 square feet of technical space, about 78 watts per square foot, which is a floor-area-rich and power-modest ratio.

For AI specifically, the same megawatt buys fewer racks as density rises. At a conservative 40 kW per rack, 19 MW supports roughly 475 racks. At the 60 to 80 kW per rack that AI training can reach, it supports 240 to 320. Capacity measured in megawatts therefore understates how much the AI question turns on delivered power rather than building size.

What the data does not cover is decisive. Nothing is published about available power, water cooling, grid interconnection timeline, or whether the 19 MW is already contracted. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities and only 19 publish capacity, so a tenth-place state ranking describes disclosure rather than deployment. The suitability score of 62 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing.
